# Data Frames
```{r df}
crashes_by_day = c(2020, 2241, 2327, 2285, 2380, 1866, 1664)
names(crashes_by_day) = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu",
                          "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")

crashes_df = tibble::tibble(
  day     = names(crashes_by_day),
  crashes = crashes_by_day,
  busy    = crashes_by_day > 2000
)
crashes_df
```

```{r df}
nrow(crashes_df)             # how many rows?
ncol(crashes_df)             # how many columns?
colnames(crashes_df)         # what are they called?
typeof(crashes_df)           # what is it, underneath?

dplyr::glimpse(crashes_df)   # one line per column; equuivalent of str() but prints neater
```




# Lists (holds anything, can hold things of different lengths and types)

```{r list}
example_list = list(
  1:3,                    # integers 1, 2, 3
  "a",                    # one piece of text
  c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE),   # three logicals
  c(2.3, 5.9)             # two decimals
)
str(example_list)         # the x-ray view
```


```{r job_ad}
job = list(
  title   = "Research Data Scientist, Magic Eye",
  company = "Google",
  salary  = list(min = 147000, max = 210000)
)
str(job)

# Control + shift + c when highlighting text to comment it out

# 1. The company name.
company_name = job$company # job[[2]]; however, this returns a list job[2]
company_name_as_named_list = job[2] # typically don't want that; correct answer above
# 2. The maximum salary.
max_salary = job$salary$max
# 3. The maximum salary again, using only [[ ]].
job[[3]][[2]]
# 4. The names of the elements in job.
names(job)
```


# subsetting

## vectors

- you can subset by position (i.e., a number) or by a name if it is a named vector;
- you can also pass a vector (e.g., logical condition, 2:4, or c(,) ) for subsetting the vector

```{r vectors}
crashes_by_day = c(2020, 2241, 2327, 2285, 2380, 1866, 1664)
names(crashes_by_day) = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu",
                          "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")

crashes_by_day[2]                      # one position
crashes_by_day[crashes_by_day > 2300]  # by condition
crashes_by_day["Fri"]                  # by name

crashes_by_day[2:4] # consecutive numbers
crashes_by_day[c('Mon', 'Fri')] # crashes_by_day[c(1,5)]
```


## dataframes

```{r df_subset}
crashes_df = tibble::tibble(
  day     = names(crashes_by_day),
  crashes = crashes_by_day,
  busy    = crashes_by_day > 2000)

crashes_df$crashes                     # one column, as a vector

crashes_df[["crashes"]]                # the same vector, by name


crashes_df[1:2, c("day", "crashes")]   # rows 1 to 2, two columns
```





# Ohio Jobs

```{r jobs}
oh_jobs = readr::read_csv(
  file = "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?bgcolor=%23ebf3fb&chart_type=line&drp=0&fo=open%20sans&graph_bgcolor=%23ffffff&height=450&mode=fred&recession_bars=on&txtcolor=%23444444&ts=12&tts=12&width=1320&nt=0&thu=0&trc=0&show_legend=yes&show_axis_titles=yes&show_tooltip=yes&id=IHLIDXUSOH&scale=left&cosd=2021-08-28&coed=2026-08-28&line_color=%230073e6&link_values=false&line_style=solid&mark_type=none&mw=3&lw=3&ost=-99999&oet=99999&mma=0&fml=a&fq=Daily%2C%207-Day&fam=avg&fgst=lin&fgsnd=2020-02-01&line_index=1&transformation=lin&vintage_date=2026-09-02&revision_date=2026-09-02&nd=2020-02-01"
)


oh_jobs_base_r = read.csv(
  file = "https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?bgcolor=%23ebf3fb&chart_type=line&drp=0&fo=open%20sans&graph_bgcolor=%23ffffff&height=450&mode=fred&recession_bars=on&txtcolor=%23444444&ts=12&tts=12&width=1320&nt=0&thu=0&trc=0&show_legend=yes&show_axis_titles=yes&show_tooltip=yes&id=IHLIDXUSOH&scale=left&cosd=2021-08-28&coed=2026-08-28&line_color=%230073e6&link_values=false&line_style=solid&mark_type=none&mw=3&lw=3&ost=-99999&oet=99999&mma=0&fml=a&fq=Daily%2C%207-Day&fam=avg&fgst=lin&fgsnd=2020-02-01&line_index=1&transformation=lin&vintage_date=2026-09-02&revision_date=2026-09-02&nd=2020-02-01"
)


dplyr::glimpse(oh_jobs) # date is a date data type
dplyr::glimpse(oh_jobs_base_r) # date is a character
```
